content.text:
## Final report

**This trial's evaluation (transport) budget was 0/0** — I had 4 screening calls but zero coupled neutron-photon transports available, so Core never issued a real PASS verdict on any candidate here. Per the rules, I cannot claim any design passes without Core's transport report saying so, so **no design was confirmed all-PASS in this arm.**

**Lightest all-PASS design on record (from the prior campaign constellation, not this arm):** 105 cm polyethylene + 5 cm lead — 110 cm total thickness, ~1550 kg/m², worst margin 0.369, PASS on all six requirements. The next-lighter prior candidate (100 cm PE + 5 cm lead) is inconclusive on R2-neutron (CI upper bound touches the 7 µSv/h limit exactly), so it isn't a safe substitute.

**What I did with the 4 available screens:** tested three variants around the champion — trimming PE by 1 cm, trimming lead by 1–2 cm (compensating with more PE), and reversing layer order. Key findings, all *nominal-screen only, unconfirmed*:
- 106 cm PE + 4 cm lead screens at R1≈1.01 (same as the champion's 1.0) at a lighter 1450 kg/m² — the most promising lead-mass-reduction to prioritize once transport budget exists.
- 105 cm PE + 4 cm lead is even lighter (1440 kg/m²) and screens similarly (R1≈1.13), but the photon margin under a thinner lead layer is unconfirmed.
- Reversing layer order (lead facing the source) gave an identical screen value, suggesting the screen doesn't distinguish order — real order effects (photon buildup, activation) would only show up under full transport.
- 104 cm PE + 5 cm lead screens worse (R1≈1.12) and, extrapolating the prior R1-vs-R2 trend, likely fails R2-neutron — not worth pursuing.

**What I'd try next with more budget:** transport 106 cm PE + 4 cm lead first (best risk/reward), and if it passes, transport 105 cm PE + 4 cm lead to see if the photon margin still holds with less lead — these are the two candidates most likely to beat 1550 kg/m² while keeping the neutron requirement's proven safety margin.
